title: Her books, Mrs. Le Breton and language classes
summary: They discuss her old books and a book on Indians by Mrs. Le Breton, then her languages class with several teachers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you bring all of your books over, all of those books that you used to have over on St. Philip Street, did you bring them all over here?
No, I had no place to put nothing, nothing, nothing. I brought nothing but myself here.
You didn't throw those books out, I hope, did you?
I know you had all sorts of books.
What was that one book you showed me once about the American Indians? Some friend of yours wrote a book on the... Oh.
Uh, uh, Hataima. George has got it. Oh, you had that issues.
I forgot what that book was. I know you showed it to us one day.
Yes, Miss, Miss, Le Breton, Le Breton, her name. But it's Le Breton in French. So she took 42, if not longer than that, to write that book.
Well, she taught at Newcomb, didn't she? Hmm? She taught at Newcomb College, didn't she?

They still, they don't teach no more now. But they, I don't know what they are, there's something in that Newcomb and Tulane and Loyola, Loyola as they call it. Yes. Oh, those are smart people. Hmm. Hmm.
Oh, you're not taking a picture of me, I hope. No, no. No, no.

It's going to get out of the way, huh? Yeah, I think it was a deep bit. When Dick was patting you, he was one of those smart people, you see. He's one of those smart people that he's lying, I had to pat him on the back.
That's when we get out of the way. How many different languages could you read? Did you read German to you?

They read it to me. I was like all young people, foolish, giggling, wouldn't pay attention, wouldn't. But, you know, W.W. King. Yes. Gracie King. Yes. You know, they had a class all the week, every other day I believe, where Herman Gessner, which the one teaching there must be his grandson, and then Mrs. Verar and Charles Gaiare. Oh, yes. Mrs. Gerard and Charles Gaiare was French, and Capitaine de Chivarria was for Spanish, and Herman Gessner was German. So every other day they had a class, ladies would be there, Mrs. Schafferri, Mrs. LaDue, Mrs. Sam, Sam, S-E-M-M-E-S. They'd be together and they'd have, just like we're talking now, and they speak nothing but that language of the class that did to me. And I used to laugh, ask me for water and tell me thank you or something like that. So one day Mrs. Gracie told me, little girl, you have an opportunity of learning what you'll never be able to pay for. And then I reflect all that evening. I say, well, after all, Mrs. Gracie is right. I can't pay no Spanish, what's the name, teacher, neither German, French are no all right. So I begin, I begin to pay, just spoke Spanish, Capitaine de Chivarria was a Spaniard.
